summary: Louisa, VA 100-ft Aermotor on Virginia Department of Forestry grounds; NHLR dates it 1944 to the CCC, at odds with the CCC's 1933-1942 run; NHLR-registered 1995.

facts.design: 100-foot Aermotor tower with a 7-by-7-foot steel cab

access.note: Beside a Department of Forestry building. The 2019 visit report describes that office as unmanned, with a sign listing phone numbers for assistance. No visitor rules found.

events.note: NHLR gives 1944, built by the CCC for the Virginia Forest Service. Conflicts with the CCC's 1933-1942 run (Wikipedia); treat as disputed
Visit report dated August 9, 2019 (James Hull): fresh paint, intact windows, stairs not judgeable remotely, tower not staffed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Left open. NHLR gives 1944 and credits the CCC, but Wikipedia dates the CCC to 1933-1942 and the 1991 state survey ties its tower count to the CCC era. The story reports 1944 as the Register's date and flags it as disputed.

sources.title: Survey of State-Owned Properties, Virginia Department of Forestry (1991)

notes_for_editor: Build year and builder rest on one register entry that conflicts with the CCC's dates; no second source found. The CCC Company 2359 article from The Central Virginian turned up in search but returned 404 on fetch, so it is not cited. The Louisa County 1995 survey was checked and does not mention the tower. Access is inferred from the 2019 visit report, not a current source. The NHLR page lists the Virginia Department of Forestry as both administrator and cooperator, which confirms the record's agency. The Register's claim that this is the only such tower in Virginia is not repeated because it is unverified. A Facebook post placing the tower off West Main St was not used. Height converted from 100 ft. Consider adding a built event as an editor's call; the record had none.
